chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said:
I asked him about the purchase of al-khiyanah and al-sariqah, so he said: 'If you know that it is so, then there is no issue except that it be something you buy from the workers.'

key_terms.السَّرِقَةِ: Al-sariqah (often used in trade contexts to denote uncertainty or hidden defects)
key_terms.الْخِيَانَةِ: Al-khiyanah (a specific type of commercial uncertainty or defect in goods)
key_terms.الْعُمَّالِ: Al-'ammal (workers/laborers, often implying direct purchase from the source of production)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying goods with uncertainty (gharar) from workers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of buying *al-khiyanah* (uncertainty/guarantee) and *al-sariqah* (robbery/theft) by distinguishing between general uncertainty and specific knowledge of the defect. He permits the transaction if the buyer is aware of the condition, particularly when purchasing from workers or producers, thereby linking the ruling to the principle of *gharar* (excessive uncertainty) in commercial law. This highlights the Shia juristic approach of validating transactions where the core uncertainty is known and accepted by both parties.
